beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Love is easy to picture at the beginning. A man and a woman, hands joined, a covenant freely given, a home with the door open and the road ahead warm. That is how God's love for his people began.

timing.text: Love is easy to picture at the beginning.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: But she wandered. Not because he stopped being good to her — he never did — but because her heart drifted. And Hosea wrote down what she told herself as she went.

timing.text: But she wandered.

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink.

timing.text: I will go after my lovers, that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oil and my drink.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I am going after the ones who give me what I want, she said. My food, my water, my clothes. She did not think she was walking away from love. She thought she was walking toward it — down the long road toward the cold lights of somewhere else.

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: Go yet, love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress, according to the love of the LORD toward the children of Israel, who look to other gods.

timing.text: Go yet, love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress, according to the love of the LORD toward the children of Israel, who look to other gods.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And here the story stops being like any other. God did not tell Hosea to forget her. Go and love her still, he said — love her the very way I love a people who leave me. The whole marriage was a picture of God's own heart, acted out by a man who had to live it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: By the time he found where she had ended up, she had lost nearly everything. Brought low, sitting at the edge of a far marketplace, poor and unseen — a long way from the home she left.

timing.text: By the time he found where she had ended up, she had lost nearly everything.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He could have let her stay lost. Instead he came looking. He walked all that way into a place that was not his own, searching the crowd for the one face he had never stopped loving.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley.

timing.text: So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And when he found her, he did not lecture her. He paid for her.

timing.text: And when he found her, he did not lecture her.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He lifted her up off the ground with his own hands, drew his cloak around her shoulders, and covered her — no shame thrown at her, no debt held over her, only welcome. She was his again, not because she earned it, but because he paid.

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I will win her back, God says. I will take her out where it is quiet, away from all the noise, and I will speak to her tenderly. Not shouting. Not shaming. Speaking comfortably — the way you talk to someone you are glad to have back.

beats.speaker: woman
beats.text: I will go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now.

timing.text: I will go and return to my first husband; for then was it better with me than now.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is the whole of repentance in one honest sentence. Turning around on the road and heading home.

timing.text: That is the whole of repentance in one honest sentence.

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies. I will even betroth thee unto me in faithfulness: and thou shalt know the LORD.

timing.text: And I will betroth thee unto me forever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Betrothed for ever. Not taken back on probation — married again, in righteousness and mercy and faithfulness, for good. That is what God says to everyone sure they have wandered too far to be wanted back. He does not wait at the door with a list of your failures. He comes looking, he pays the price himself, and he calls you home.

card.text: God dramatized his own love with a marriage: however far she wandered, he went and bought her back and brought her home. You are not too far gone to be wanted. What would it mean to be loved home like that?
